help:
usage: oms graph [-h] [--repo REPO] [--pretty] [--version] {project,exec} ...

Project graph and execution graph over the existing OMS control plane.

positional arguments:
  {project,exec}
    project       structural code graph: build, query, blast radius, context
                  packs
    exec          advanced opt-in execution graph; ordinary work uses existing
                  plans/autopilot

options:
  -h, --help      show this help message and exit
  --repo REPO     project repository or directory; later values override
                  earlier ones
  --pretty        pretty-print JSON
  --version       show program's version number and exit

project.help:
usage: oms graph project [-h] [--repo REPO] [--pretty]
                         {build,ensure,check,map,find,api,search,symbol,neighbors,trace,blast,coupling,unreferenced,affected,impact,context,benchmark}
                         ...

Structural code graph over --repo. State lives in <repo>/.oms/project-graph/
unless OMS_PROJECT_GRAPH_STATE names an absolute directory to use instead.
Readers build or refresh it themselves unless --no-refresh or
OMS_GRAPH_AUTOBUILD=0 says otherwise.

positional arguments:
  {build,ensure,check,map,find,api,search,symbol,neighbors,trace,blast,coupling,unreferenced,affected,impact,context,benchmark}
    api                 signatures and summaries for one indexed file, without
                        bodies
    search              exhaustive case-insensitive literal search grouped by
                        graph symbol
    symbol              one symbol's definitions, graph references and
                        unlinked text matches, in separate zones
    coupling            paths that change together in Git history;
                        structural=no marks coupling the parsers cannot see
    unreferenced        symbols with no incoming graph edge; review
                        candidates, not proof of dead code
    affected            fail-open affected-test plan for an exact Git range
    impact              one orientation brief for a Git range: affected tests,
                        dependents, co-change partners left out, CODEOWNERS

    benchmark           opt-in history recall snapshots and comparison

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo REPO           project repository or directory; later values override
                        earlier ones
  --pretty              pretty-print JSON

map.help:
usage: oms graph project map [-h] [--repo REPO] [--pretty] [--include-tests]
                             [--limit LIMIT] [--depth DEPTH] [--json]
                             [--brief] [--signatures] [--task TASK]
                             [--max-bytes MAX_BYTES] [--max-files MAX_FILES]
                             [--entry-path PATH]
                             [--html-fragment ABSOLUTE_PATH | --ui-model]
                             [--no-refresh]

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  --repo REPO           project repository or directory; later values override
                        earlier ones
  --pretty              pretty-print JSON
  --include-tests       keep test files in the overview (dropped by default)
  --limit LIMIT         maximum nodes in a visual output (1-200)
  --depth DEPTH         neighbor depth in the HTML overview (0-4)
  --json
  --brief               print the cached orientation brief (not combinable
                        with --json or visual outputs)
  --signatures          with --task: the files ranked for the task as
                        extracted signatures, inside --max-bytes (no bodies,
                        nothing written)
  --task TASK           task text ranked the same way as `context` (requires
                        --signatures)
  --max-bytes MAX_BYTES
                        byte budget of the signature text (256-262144)
  --max-files MAX_FILES
                        ranked files considered by --signatures (1-200)
  --entry-path PATH     with --signatures: anchor to an exact repo-relative
                        file; repeatable
  --html-fragment ABSOLUTE_PATH
                        write a bounded interactive HTML fragment for an agent
                        UI
  --ui-model            emit the bounded graph data consumed by an MCP Apps
                        renderer
  --no-refresh          read the graph as it stands; never build or refresh it
